newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Macau air cargo gains, container traffic up.
newsitem.headline: Macau air cargo gains, container traffic up.

text.p: The number of containers being shipped between Hong Kong to Macau to feed air freighters rising steadily, the airport's cargo centre manager, Michael Hanley told Reuters.

The use of barges to ferry containers around 40 miles between Hong Kong and Macau was pioneered last year by SAS to feed its newly inaugurated freighter service from the tiny Portuguese enclave. Since then other cargo carriers, such as South Korea's Asiana Airlines, have followed suit.

"The use of containers is working very well and trade is growing in both directions," Hanley said. The main in-bound commodities to Macau are machine tools and raw materials, Hanley said. The main export from Macau is clothing mainly bound for Hong Kong's shopping malls.
He was speaking as the Macau International Airport Company (CAM) published latest monthly figures which showed 3,342 tonnes of cargo was handled during May, a increase of 210 tonnes over April.
"For the year to date we have seen an increase over last year of around 220 per cent in terms of actual pounds loaded and that is a good sign for us," Hanley added.
Hanley said he was confident of more cargo flights being attracted to Macau later this year but declined to give further details.
